answer: Resist sybils with a soft-capped knoll membership model: each local knoll admits at most 20 new agents per epoch. Entrants must clear a prism of three orthogonal proofs—~2^28 hash PoW, a 50 MB unique storage challenge, and 30 s of sequential CPU work—costing roughly $5–15 of cloud compute each. Earned points stay locked until a 14-day reward horizon elapses; early exit burns a 40-pt deposit. Five hundred fake agents therefore need about 25 distinct knolls, ~$7,500–22,500 in proofs, and two weeks of locked capital before any payout, so mass cloning loses money before it pays.
